name: Kids Abroad
person: The Adeyemi household — child to a UK university
story: The rocket line. The degree is priced in pounds, and the naira collapsed ₦460 → ₦2,050/£ mid-journey — so every instalment ballooned. ₦66.3m spent: more than the other four dreams combined.
caveat: The steep rise is NOT compounding or success — it is the exchange rate inflating the cost of the same degree. A shock wearing the costume of growth.

milestones.item: Tobi in SS2 -- abroad plan begins, dedicated saving starts
Sells a land plot in Mowe to fund the deposit
UK student visa + IHS granted; deposit paid
One-way flight Lagos to London booked
Takes N3m cooperative loan for the Year-2 gap
Exchange rate collapses -- naira tuition nearly doubles
Final-year tuition -- deepest strain; N4m coop loan #2
Tobi GRADUATES -- the dream is achieved
Arc ends -- success, but deep in debt, land gone
